# About the Role
As an Associate Director, Analytics, you will lead complex analytics and data science engagements, bringing together strong quantitative expertise, strategic thinking, and client leadership.
This role requires a strong foundation in data science and advanced analytics.
You should be comfortable working with sophisticated analytical methodologies, evaluating data science approaches and outputs, and translating complex quantitative findings into clear business recommendations.
At the Associate Director level, you will also lead teams and workstreams, influence senior stakeholders, and help shape the analytical approach to complex client challenges.
You may not be coding or building models every day, but you should have sufficient data science depth to credibly guide the work and challenge the methodology.
# Responsibilities
# Data Science & Advanced Analytics
Lead advanced analytics and data science work across complex client engagements.
Apply and guide approaches such as statistical modeling, predictive analytics, experimentation, segmentation, forecasting, machine learning, or other advanced quantitative methodologies as appropriate to the business problem.
Evaluate analytical approaches and outputs, identify limitations and opportunities, and ensure that methodologies are rigorous, actionable, and connected to client objectives.
# Complex Program & Engagement Leadership
Lead complex analytics projects or programs end to end across one or more accounts—shaping the analytical approach, orchestrating cross-functional teams, and owning outcomes at a senior level.
# Strategic Analytics & Client Advisory
Translate sophisticated analysis and data science outputs into clear business implications and recommendations.
Connect analytical findings to the client's broader marketing and business agenda.
Serve as a senior analytics partner to clients and internal stakeholders, helping frame ambiguous business questions into analytical problems that can be solved with data.
# Team & Technical Leadership
Lead and develop analytics and data science talent, set expectations for analytical quality, and provide guidance on methodologies and approaches across multiple workstreams.
Partner effectively with data scientists, analysts, media teams, strategists, engineers, and other specialists to deliver integrated solutions.
# Early Account Economics
Take first-line accountability for the economics of your workstreams—including utilization, scope discipline, and margin within your remit—and partner with account leadership on planning and resourcing.
# Client Advisory & Growth
Build credible senior client relationships and identify opportunities where analytics, data science, measurement, or AI capabilities can address additional client needs.
# AI-Enabled Delivery & Innovation
Identify qualified AI use cases and opportunities to incorporate AI-enabled approaches into analytics and measurement.
Help evaluate where emerging technologies can create measurable value rather than applying AI for its own sake.
# About You
# The Essentials
- 7+ years of experience in analytics, data science, quantitative consulting, measurement, or a related field across an agency, consultancy, holding company, technology company, or sophisticated in-house environment
- Demonstrated data science experience is required, with a strong understanding of advanced quantitative methodologies such as statistical modeling, predictive analytics, experimentation, machine learning, forecasting, segmentation, or related approaches
- Experience leading complex analytics or data science projects from business problem definition through analysis, interpretation, and recommendation
- Ability to evaluate and guide sophisticated analytical work, including methodology, assumptions, limitations, and business implications
- Ability to translate complex quantitative findings into clear, actionable recommendations for non-technical and senior audiences
- Experience partnering with or leading data scientists, analysts, and other technical specialists
- Experience leading and developing teams
- Demonstrated influence across functions, client teams, or portfolios
- Credible senior client relationships and the ability to advise, not just deliver
- Emerging account-economics literacy, including utilization, scope, and margin within a remit
# Strong Plus
- Hands-on experience with programming and analytical tools such as SQL, Python, R, or similar
- Experience with experimentation, causal inference, marketing measurement, incrementality, attribution, or other advanced measurement approaches
- Experience applying machine learning or predictive modeling to marketing or business problems
- Experience integrating GenAI or agentic platforms with measurable outcomes
- Quantified contribution to account growth or scope expansion
- Recognized domain authority through frameworks, methodologies, or thought leadership
- Experience developing reusable analytical methodologies, tools, or accelerators
- Senior platform partnership experience with Google, Meta, Adobe, Amazon, or similar
- Cross-domain experience across more than one IMA practice area

# About the role
Muon Space is hiring a Product Manager to own how much data our missions get to the ground, and how we prove it.
Reporting to a Director of Product Management, you will own bits-to-ground communications across RF and optical links, simulation, and software test.
This position is hybrid and requires working on-site in our San Jose, CA office four days per week.
# Responsibilities
# Comms, Simulation and Test
- Own the product roadmap for bits-to-ground communications across RF and optical (OCT) links.
- Own the product roadmap for Muon Sim, the digital twin behind mission design and mission operations, including the throughput analysis that sets what a constellation can deliver.
- Grow simulation into a tool for software iteration, so flight and ground software can be exercised against the twin before it reaches a spacecraft.
- Own the product roadmap for software test infrastructure, automation, and hardware-in-the-loop environments.
- Define and prioritize features that improve product quality, schedule adherence, or customer value.
- Author clear Product Requirements Documents (PRDs), drive alignment, and follow through reliably.
- Partner with the Director of Product Management to develop the strategy for the product areas including build/buy decisions.
- Conduct customer interviews, gather feedback on product–market fit, and translate insights into roadmap decisions.
# Cross-functional Coordination
- Partner closely with engineering teams across ground software, simulation, test, and mission systems to define features and roadmap.
- Partner with other software product managers on roadmaps where capabilities intersect.
- Coordinate with the Director of PM — Federal on defense-aligned product needs and inputs to roadmap.
- Collaborate with the VP of Product and the broader PM team on strategic roadmap decisions and prioritization trade-offs.
# Required Qualifications
- 3–5 years of Product Management experience, with demonstrated success owning software products in technically complex environments.
- Experience in communications systems, simulation, test infrastructure, or adjacent deep-tech software domains.
- Experience working cross-functionally with multiple engineering teams at once, rather than a single team.
- Demonstrated success in uncertain environments with incomplete requirements and shifting schedules.
- Proven track record delivering major features or programs spanning multiple months of effort.
- History of independent execution and implementation across multiple concurrent workstreams.
- Strong fluency working with engineering peers and leadership; able to influence cross-organizational technical investment without direct authority.
- Demonstrated ability to translate customer mission needs into detailed product requirements and acceptance criteria across software systems.
- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field; advanced degree preferred.
# Nice-to-have Skills
- Active U.S. Government security clearance.
- Familiarity with RF or optical communications, link budgets, or ground station networks.
- Familiarity with mission design, constellation modeling, or digital-twin platforms across orbit, power, and data delivery.
- Familiarity with test automation or hardware-in-the-loop test environments.
- Familiarity with building or operating software for the space environment.
- Prior experience in startup or high-growth technology environments.
# Salary
The salary range for this role is $190,000-$210,000, plus a competitive equity grant and comprehensive benefits package.
Final compensation will be determined based on skills, qualifications, experience, and geographic location as assessed during the interview process.
> # About Muon Space
> Founded in 2021, Muon Space is an end-to-end Space Systems Provider that designs, builds, and operates LEO satellite constellations delivering mission-critical data.
> Our revolutionary, integrated technology stack enables customers to optimize every dimension of their missions for faster time-to-orbit and superior constellation remote sensing performance.
> Our state-of-the-art facility in the heart of Silicon Valley is optimized for manufacturing spacecraft and rapid, flexible payload integration at scale.
> From climate monitoring to national security, Muon Space is dedicated to delivering Earth Intelligence for a safer and more resilient world.
> # Taking Care of Our Team
> At Muon salary is only part of our total compensation package.
> In addition to salary, full-time employees receive equity compensation as well as benefits including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k retirement plan, short & long term disability and life insurance.
> We also offer three weeks paid vacation for new employees, along with 12 paid holidays, unlimited sick time and paid parental leave.
> Our mission embraces the entire planet and we believe our team should too.
> Muon is dedicated to creating a diverse and dynamic company and workforce.
> We believe in equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, age, national origin, citizenship, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, or gender identity.
> We value diversity in the workplace, and that starts with our applicants.
> We encourage you to apply, even if you don't check all the boxes, and we look forward to reviewing your application!
> In addition, if you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know.
> Muon is currently registered and able to hire in the following states:
> AL, AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, FL, GA, IL, IA, ID, MD, MA, MI, MN, MO, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OR, PA, TN, TX, VT, VA, WA

Title: Community Engagement Manager Data Centres Canada
Title reason: SCOPE_AMBIGUITY

> # About Anthropic
> Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.
> We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole.
> Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
# About the role
Anthropic is building AI systems that will shape the trajectory of one of the most consequential technologies in human history.
That work requires physical infrastructure at significant scale, and building that infrastructure the right way means being a real, long-term partner to the communities where we operate.
We are looking for a Community Engagement Manager in Canada to join our Public Policy team and serve as Anthropic's on-the-ground presence in the communities where our data centres are sited, built, and operated.
This is not a communications role or a government affairs role, though you will do elements of both.
It is a relationship role: your job is to make Anthropic a trusted, visible, and valued neighbour, from the earliest stages of site selection through construction and long-term operations.
You will be the connective tissue between Anthropic's Policy and Infrastructure teams and the local officials, community organizations, economic development partners, and residents who have a stake in what we build.
You will surface concerns before they escalate, translate our technical and operational plans into clear local benefits, and build the coalitions that allow us to move quickly and responsibly.
Because Anthropic's infrastructure footprint is still early in its growth, you will also help write the playbook: the processes you build in your first markets are the ones we will use as we expand.
You will travel regularly within your region, up to 50% of the time, and occasionally to other Anthropic data centre markets.
# Key responsibilities
- Build and maintain trusted, sustained relationships with municipal governments, both elected and unelected, provincial ministers and agencies, economic development organizations, community groups, civic leaders, educational institutions, and workforce partners in the data centre markets you cover
- Develop and execute a community engagement strategy for each of your markets, spanning site selection, pre-development, construction, and ongoing operations
- Build external coalitions, host education and listening sessions, and design local solutions that deliver real benefits to the communities where we operate
- Represent Anthropic in public forums, town halls, planning hearings, community events, and local media
- Monitor community sentiment and local political dynamics, and advise internal teams on risks, opportunities, and the right pace and posture for engagement
- Partner with the Real Estate and Infrastructure team to bring community input into how projects are planned, communicated, and delivered, not just how they are announced
- Work with the Communications team to develop proactive, locally relevant messaging
- Coordinate charitable giving, community investment, and economic development commitments in your markets, including managing nonprofit partner relationships
- Partner with the Energy and Sustainability team to explain our approach to environmental stewardship and respond to questions about power, water, and land use
- Build a community engagement playbook and repeatable processes that scale as Anthropic's infrastructure footprint grows
# Minimum qualifications
- Experience in community affairs, public affairs, economic development, government relations, municipal or provincial government, or a closely related field
- Direct experience working for or engaging with municipal governments, both elected councils and administration, and provincial government on behalf of large infrastructure, construction, energy, or technology projects, with a working understanding of how local politics and community dynamics actually play out
- A skilled relationship and coalition builder who earns trust with a diverse group of stakeholders, and who maintains relationships through difficult conversations
- The ability to represent a company credibly in public settings — town halls, hearings, press interviews
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to turn a complex operational plan into plain language that a local official or reporter can understand and respond to
- The ability to work independently, get up to speed quickly on complex policy issues, and manage multiple concurrent engagements across different markets without losing track of any of them
- Based in Alberta, Canada or willing to relocate there, and prepared to travel regularly across the region
# Preferred qualifications
- 7+ years of experience in community engagement specifically on data centre, utility, energy, or large-scale industrial infrastructure projects, or in local government
- Familiarity with land use, zoning, and development permitting processes at the municipal and provincial level
- Experience managing corporate social responsibility programs
- Established relationships with economic development, workforce, or civic organizations in the markets this role covers
- Experience working with real estate, legal, communications, and policy teams at the same time
- A genuine interest in the communities where you work, not just the projects you are managing
> # Logistics
> Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience
> Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience
> Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position
> Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time.
> However, some roles may require more time in our offices.
> Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas!
> However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate.
> But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.
> We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
> Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.
> Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work.
> We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications.
> We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.
> Your safety matters to us.
> To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses.
> In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic.
> Be cautious of emails from other domains.
> Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day.
> If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.
> # How we're different
> We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science.
> At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts.
> And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles.
> We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science.
> We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time.
> As such, we greatly value communication skills.
> The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research.
> This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.
> # Come work with us!
> Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco.
> We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues.
> Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.
